newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS -Baht hit by dollar rise,weak stocks.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS -Baht hit by dollar rise,weak stocks.

text.p: The Thai baht came under renewed pressure from a surging dollar/yen and poor sentiment on the local stock market, dealers said on Thursday.

The baht was quoted at 25.971-25.976 to the dollar at 0415 GMT against 25.927/25.933 late on Wednesday. The Bank of Thailand (BOT) fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.90, its lowest level since June 1990, and against 25.89 on Wednesday.
"There were very active bids for dollar this morning. Sentiment on the baht was relatively weak following the stock market plunge yesterday," said a foreign bank dealer in Bangkok.
The Thai SET Index lost nearly three percent on Wednesday, partly on reports of an interest payment default by a major property company, brokers said.

"News on interest payment default by a property firm also triggered concern in the foreign exchange market about positions of commercial banks and finance companies," said another senior dealer at a local bank.
"Banks and finance companies have large loan exposure to the property sector," he said.
Dealers said the government's reduction of its 1997 trade deficit forecast to 413 billion baht from 595 billion earlier did not help sentiment.
A senior dealer with a Thai bank in Singapore said there had been no sign of intervention by the BOT on Thursday despite the fact that the baht was trading outside the central bank's band.
"I don't think they will come in until we all go on a long weekend. Without the Hong Kong and Singapore players around, they can determine where they want the rate to be," he said.

The Thai overnight interbank rate shot to a new six-month high of 19.00-20.00 percent in early trade due to strong demand for funds for the Lunar New Year and the central bank's reserve requirement on Friday.
Elsewhere, the Singapore dollar remained weak but had recovered from its low of S$1.4145 to the U.S. dollar after the previous day's sell-off by a large U.S. fund.
Dealers said activity was very subdued with most banks preparing to close early on the eve of a four-day break for the Chinese and Moslem new years.
"There's buying interest in dollar/Sing at 1.4120 and selling at 1.4140. It'll depend on the dollar/majors, but I prefer the upside," said a European bank dealer.
He said there was also a lot of corporate buying interest for the U.S. dollar below S$1.4100 and a breach of the S$1.4150 resistance would put it on track for S$1.4200.

In Malaysia, the ringgit was similarly afflicted by two-way trading interest and thin market conditions, but dealers said it was likely to remain underpinned by buying interest in the ringgit/Sing cross.
"We're capped in a range but it looks like the market is more keen to buy the ringgit/Sing since this is what both central banks want," said the European bank dealer.
The Thai bank dealer said the dollar was likely to be well supported at its previous resistance of 2.4900 ringgit.
Dealers said the ringgit could be in for some volatility in a thin holiday market. Malaysian banks are closed from Friday through Tuesday for the festivals.
"If 2.48 to 2.50 range is broken, a lot of stops would break on both sides," said another European bank dealer in Singapore.
The Indonesian rupiah was relatively stable as activity dwindled in the spot market due to the absence of offshore parties and ahead of holidays in Jakarta.
Spot rupiah was at 2,376.50/77.00 at 0415 GMT against an opening of 2,377.5/78.0.
The Jakarta foreign exchange market will be closed for Eid al-Fitr on February 10 and 11 inclusive, while the stock market will be closed from February 7 to 11 inclusive.
Dealers in Jakarta said the focus was on the swap market, with foreign players seen heavily short-covering in short-term swaps.
"Offshore players are maintaining long dollar positions as they anticipate the central bank might be forced to buy dollars in the near future," said a local bank dealer.

He said an intervention from the bank would result in fresh rupiah injection which might drive swap rates down. This would cause players to establish short positions in long-term swaps in advance while covering them with short-term commitments.
